key: Move far from me what sins I have committed: let me not suffer, King, for guilt of others. Full many a morn remains to dawn upon us: in these, O Varuna, while we live direct us.
s: Late in a hymn to Varuna, the verse follows praise of his unmoving statutes; Sāyaṇa, on 2.28.8, reads the sins as debts, his forebears’ and his own, and the undawned mornings as dawns that seem not to break for a debtor awake before daylight.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 2.28.8 (his verse 9), sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 208788 (2019)

evidence.words: हे वरुण ऋणा ऋणानि पित्रादिभिः कृतान्यस्माभिर्देयानि परासावीः परासुव पराचीनं प्रेरय प्रेरणे छान्दुसोलुङ् अध अधुना मत्कृतानि मया निष्पादितानि ऋणानि परासुव अपि च हे राजन् स्वामिन् वरुण अहं अन्यकृतेन अन्यैरर्जितेन धनेन मा भोजं भोगं मा लभेयम् किं कारणमिति चेदुच्यते - भूयसीः भूयस्यो बहुतराः उषसः अव्युष्टा इत्नु सत्यं अव्युष्टा एव अपररात्रेषूत्थाय ऋणानि चिन्तयतो जाग्रतो मम व्युष्टा अप्यव्युष्टकल्पा आसन्
evidence.gloss: O Varuna, ṛṇā, debts: the debts made by fathers and others, which we must pay, parāsāvīḥ, drive away, send off (an irregular aorist of impelling); adha, now: those made by me, the debts I have incurred, drive away. And, O King, lord Varuna, let me not enjoy by wealth earned by others. Why? Many dawns were truly undawned: for me, who rise in the last part of the night and stay awake thinking of my debts, even the dawns that broke were as good as undawned.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 2.28.8, at [218,8]). Griffith joins Sāyaṇa’s verses 1 and 2, so the app’s 2.28.8 is Sāyaṇa’s 2.28.9; the packet for 2.28.9 carries the matching Sanskrit (parā ṛṇā sāvīḥ ... avyuṣṭā in nu bhūyasīr uṣāsaḥ) and his gloss: the debts are those made by fathers and others and those made by me, and the many dawns were as if undawned for one who rises in the late night and stays awake thinking of his debts; Wilson’s note reports the same. The reading is his. CORRECTED one phrase: ‘a debtor lying awake’ became ‘a debtor awake before daylight’, since Sāyaṇa has him risen (utthāya) in the last part of the night (apararātreṣu), not lying in bed. Place kept as 2.28.8 (the app’s verse, per the roster trap) with ‘his verse 9’ in src. Plain sense follows 2.28.7 (statutes fixed as on a mountain). Revision 208788 dated 2019-08-05 by the Wikisource API. entry-check ok on the corrected entry.
